Bug fixes, most of them found by running the test suite against PostgreSQL for the first time
and by a pass over the web app in Russian.

### Fixed

- **Offline reading works again on PostgreSQL.** `device_public_keys.created_at` was created as
  `TIMESTAMP` while the code reads it as a timestamp _with_ time zone. SQLite shrugs at that;
  PostgreSQL refuses to decode the column, so every offline download (`POST /media/{id}/offline`)
  answered 500 — on every server migrated to PostgreSQL since 11 September. It was the only
  timestamp column in the schema without a time zone. A migration moves it to `TIMESTAMPTZ`; on
  SQLite the migration does nothing.
- **Search finds authors again.** The web's keyword search looked at name, title and summary but
  not the writers, so typing an author's name found nothing while the same search in the mobile
  client found their books.
- **Offline reading can be granted from the web.** The `OFFLINE_READ` permission existed but
  belonged to no permission group, so the users form never drew a row for it — there was no way
  to hand it out short of the API.
- **Dates follow the interface language.** They were formatted with the operating system's
  locale, so an English macOS printed "June 14, 2026" in a Russian interface.
- **The Russian interface is Russian.** A pile of labels were hardcoded in English although the
  translations already existed: the book's ••• menu, the user stats, reading direction, the EPUB
  font controls, the metadata editor's reset, several empty states and dialogs.

### Changed

- **A failed sign-in no longer locks the account.** Upstream counts a user's failures over 24
  hours from any address and, at nine, locks the account until an administrator clears it by
  hand — which means anyone who knows a username can lock its owner out, the server owner
  included. Failures are now counted per account _and address_ over 15 minutes, and that address
  gets a 429 until the window passes. The account is never touched, so the block lifts by itself
  and nobody else is affected. `is_locked` keeps its original meaning: an administrator locked
  this account.

### Also

The whole test suite now runs against PostgreSQL as well as SQLite, which is how the offline bug
above was found. New tests cover the fork's own web features, metadata writeback into EPUB files,
series visibility, reading sessions, EPUB streaming, the offline gates, book clubs and the
authorization fixes.
